text: The finance reconciliation turned up a second, unrelated problem: the dashboard's own grand total, 1,640 churned customers, was actually higher than the Excel check's 1,580. That's not a definitions gap — that's a real bug.

The tell is the pattern itself: every single region's own number was correct, only the un-sliced grand total was wrong. That specific signature — right per slice, wrong on total — points straight at a many-to-many relationship, not a logic error.

A quick query confirms it: around sixty corporate-gifting customers are tagged to two shipping regions at once. Each gets counted once per region correctly, but summed into the grand total, those same sixty get counted twice.

The fix isn't the relationship — the region drill-down actually needs it. It's the measure: filtering over a distinct, de-duplicated customer key instead of the plain values list guarantees one evaluation per customer no matter how many regions they're tagged to.
After the fix, the grand total lands back at 1,580, matching both SQL and Excel, and every individual region's number stays exactly the same, because that part was never actually broken.

A one-line comment goes right above the measure explaining why that distinct key matters here, so nobody simplifies it back into the same bug later. Next up: a third discrepancy, this time with the Python script.
